translation_notes: the two test_graph.add() calls share the subject test_subject: translated as a single +{ } with a ';'-separated predicate-object pair (rdf:type + ex:name), per the add_run_shared_subject construction.
no @prefix used: both predicates/objects are ad hoc <http://example.org/...> IRIs used once, not namespace members worth naming.

region restored out of its 'if __name__ == "__main__":' guard (dropped, body unindented one level, identically on both sides): run_pair execs the module with __name__ set to '__original__'/'__translated__', never '__main__', so under the guard as extracted nothing would run and both sides would trivially compare two empty namespaces. Same restoration and rationale as sparql_interpolated's custom_eval.py__<module>_1 (precedent).

context shims added, identical on both sides: oxigraph_shim.py replaces the real Oxigraph adapter (opens an HTTP connection to a live server) with an in-memory rdflib-backed stand-in exposing the same insert/query/get_subject_graph/remove signatures and RDF semantics; naas_abi_core/services/triple_store/resolve.py replicates the two reachable branches of resolve_local_http_url (env-var override, else default_url -- the .abi/dev/instance.json branch never triggers here); dotenv.py is a no-op load_dotenv stand-in (python-dotenv not installed).

driver applies a stdout_filter blanking 'at 0x...' addresses: the region prints row.count on a SPARQL COUNT result, but ResultRow subclasses tuple so '.count' resolves to the inherited tuple.count BOUND METHOD (a pre-existing bug in the source, not touched by translation) and printing it embeds the method object's id(), which differs run to run though the program is identical on both sides.
